definitions.meaning: A diet that covers all seven food groups in the right proportions: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water.
A food group that supplies most of the body energy, found in rice, bread and potatoes.
A food group used for growth and repair of body cells, found in meat, fish, eggs and beans.
The food group that releases the most energy per gram, about 37 kJ per gram.
The breakdown of large food molecules into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed.
The tube running from mouth to large intestine along which food is digested and absorbed.
A biological catalyst that speeds up digestion; each enzyme breaks down one nutrient.
The enzyme that breaks down starch into sugars.
The enzyme that breaks down protein into amino acids.
The enzyme that breaks down fat into fatty acids and glycerol.
Tiny finger-like projections lining the small intestine that absorb digested nutrients into the blood.
The taking of digested nutrients through the gut wall into the blood.

mechanismSteps: Seven groups: a balanced diet covers carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water in the right proportions (s1).
Food is fuel: carbohydrate and protein release about 17 kJ per gram while fat releases about 37 kJ per gram (s2).
The pipeline: food travels mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, one stage at each stop (s3).
Enzymes at work: amylase breaks down starch, protease breaks down protein and lipase breaks down fat (s4).
Absorption: the villi of the small intestine pass digested nutrients into the blood (s5).
Not the stomach: digestion continues past the stomach and finishes in the small intestine, where most absorption happens (s6).
objectives: Name the seven food groups of a balanced diet and compare the energy values per gram
Trace food through the alimentary canal and match each enzyme to its nutrient
Explain why digestion continues in the small intestine and how villi absorb nutrients
subject: science
title: Nutrition: balanced diet and digestion

trap.explanation: The slip: The stomach gets all the attention, so it feels like the last stop. The fix: Digestion does not end in the stomach: it continues in the small intestine, where most absorption happens. In class, replay the myth scene: follow one bite past the stomach and list what still happens - enzymes finish the breakdown and the villi absorb - before letting anyone call it finished.

workedExample: Test the stomach claim on the sandwich. Step 1 (s3): the bite passes mouth, oesophagus and stomach, which churns it into a liquid and only starts the breakdown. Step 2 (s6): in the small intestine, enzymes finish breaking down starch, protein and fat, and the villi absorb the products into the blood. Digestion therefore finishes in the small intestine, not in the stomach.
